key_concepts: Chemical bonding involves sharing or transferring valence electrons
Valence electrons are the outermost electrons involved in bonding
Ions are atoms or groups of atoms with a positive or negative charge
Ions form when atoms lose or gain electrons
Metals tend to lose electrons while nonmetals tend to gain electrons
The octet rule states atoms become stable with eight valence electrons
Cations are positively charged ions formed by losing electrons
Anions are negatively charged ions formed by gaining electrons
Lewis Electron Dot Structures use element symbols and dots to show valence electrons
Ionic compounds form when a metal transfers electrons to a nonmetal
Chemical formulas of ionic compounds can be written using ion charges
The crisscross method uses ion charges as subscripts to write formulas
